purpose: This medication is used to relieve headaches, including migraines, as well as general pain like muscle aches and minor arthritis discomfort. It combines three ingredients that work together to give you stronger pain relief than any one of them could provide alone. It is especially popular for tension headaches and migraines.
how_it_works: Acetaminophen and aspirin both reduce pain and fever through slightly different pathways in your body — together they tackle pain from more than one angle. Aspirin also helps reduce inflammation, which can be a cause of headache pain. The caffeine acts as a helper ingredient that actually boosts the effectiveness of the other two pain relievers, so you get better relief with smaller doses.
common_side_effects: Some people may experience an upset stomach, nausea, or heartburn, mainly because of the aspirin. You might also feel a little jittery, restless, or have trouble sleeping due to the caffeine. Drinking a full glass of water with this medicine can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: Do not take more than the recommended dose, as too much acetaminophen can seriously harm your liver. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication. Do not give aspirin to children or teenagers who have the flu, chickenpox, or viral illness, as it can cause a rare but serious condition called Reye's syndrome. If you are pregnant, nursing, have stomach ulcers, bleeding problems, kidney or liver issues, or are sensitive to caffeine, talk to your doctor before taking this. Be careful about taking other products that also contain acetaminophen or aspirin at the same time.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older, the usual dose is 2 tablets taken with a full glass of water. You can repeat this every 6 hours as needed, but do not take more than 8 tablets in a 24-hour period. Do not use for more than 10 days for pain or 3 days for fever without checking with your doctor.
